The '''1956 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship''' was the 70th staging of the All-Ireland [[hurling]] championship since its establishment by the [[Gaelic Athletic Association]] in 1887. The championship began on 22 April 1956 and ended on 23 September 1956.

[[Wexford GAA|Wexford]] were the [[1955 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|defending champions]], and retained their All-Ireland crown following a 2–14 to 2–8 defeat of [[Cork GAA|Cork]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.askaboutireland.ie/reading-room/sports-recreation/sport/wexford-hurling/wexford-hurling-in-the-19/all-ireland-win-1956/|title=All-Ireland win 1956|publisher=Ask About Ireland website|access-date=21 October 2013}}</ref>

==Teams==

A total of thirteen teams contested the championship, a reduction of one on the [[1955 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|previous championship]]. [[Wicklow GAA|Wicklow]] withdrew and did not field a team in the [[Leinster Senior Hurling Championship]].

===Scoring===

*Widest winning margin: '''19 points''' 
**Wexford 8–9 – 2–2 Laois  (<small>''Leinster semi-final, 10 June 1956''</small>)
*Most goals in a match: '''15''' 
**Westmeath 9–6 – 6–1 Meath (<small>''Leinster first round, 29 April 1956''</small>)
*Most points in a match: '''22''' 
**Wexford 2–14 – 2–8 Cork (<small>''All-Ireland final, 23 September 1956''</small>)
*Most goals by one team in a match: '''9''' 
**Westmeath 9–6 – 6–1 Meath (<small>''Leinster first round, 29 April 1956''</small>)
*Most goals scored by a losing team: '''6''' 
**Westmeath 9–6 – 6–1 Meath (<small>''Leinster first round, 29 April 1956''</small>)
*Most points scored by a losing team: '''12''' 
**Cork 5–9 – 2–12 Waterford (<small>''Munster quarter-final, 10 June 1956''</small>)

===Miscellaneous===

* [[Wexford GAA|Wexford]] won a third Leinster title in-a-row. It remains the only time in their history that they went undefeated in the provincial championship for three successive campaigns.
* An outbreak of [[polio]] in [[Cork (city)|Cork]] and the fear of a spread of the disease to [[Dublin]] due to an influx of Cork supporters lead to the postponement of the All-Ireland final until 23 September 1956.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.independent.ie/irish-news/deadly-polio-nightmare-of-50-years-ago-26412438.html|title=Deadly polio nightmare of 50 years ago|publisher=Irish Independent|date=28 May 2006|access-date=21 October 2013|first=Seán|last=Reilly}}</ref>
* The attendance of 83,096 at the All-Ireland final remains an all-time record.
* Wexford retained the All-Ireland title for the only time in their history. The 2–14 to 2–8 victory remained their only championship defeat of Cork until July 2016 when they did it again in the round 2 Qualifiers. ([[Cork–Wexford hurling rivalry]])
